tier_reason: Independent third-party shootout (r-lyeh Scriptorium, 525 stars) with public harness (bench.cc, run.bat, tests/fib.neko, tests/fib.lua, neko/make.bat building Neko 2.0.0 with /Ox /Oy /DNDEBUG /MT) whose row 11 shows nekovm 1.104 s against PUC Lua 1.341 s (row 12) on fib(34); not A because the CPU is given only as 'AMD A10 3.8 GHz' (no model number) and the Lua build flags are not stated.

corrections.baseline: PUC Lua 5.3.1 (the Scriptorium repo vendors lua/lua-5.3.1; the table links LuaDist/lua; build flags not stated)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Visual Studio 2015 RC where possible, Visual Studio 2013 elsewhere; Neko 2.0.0 and Boehm GC 7.2 built by neko/make.bat with cl /Ox /Oy /DNDEBUG /MT; Lua build flags not stated
corrections.workload: Recursive Fibonacci fib(34) (result 433494437). bench.cc launches each engine's command-line executable 5 times through system() and records the mean wall time per launch (process startup included); the Neko script is compiled to bytecode with nekoc before timing. The README table keeps each engine's minimum over the sessions recorded in bench.csv and scores it relative to Lua.
corrections.caveats: Single micro-benchmark (recursive fib(34)) from July 2015 on a Windows 7 AMD A10 3.8 GHz with MSVC 2013/2015 and Neko 2.0.0 vs Lua 5.3.1, so both engines are very old versions; the page says 'take it with a grain of salt'. Each figure is the mean of 5 process launches (startup included), and the table keeps the minimum over recorded sessions: bench.csv holds two sessions for Neko and Lua, and in the other one Neko took 2.458 s vs Lua 2.359 s (Neko about 4% slower), so the roughly 20% margin is not stable across runs. Lua build flags are not stated. The benchmark repo is hosted under the r-lyeh-archived account. The Neko README says 'Deprecated as of 2021-09-09 ... not actively maintained anymore' (compatibility fixes only), although commits continue (last 2026-09-19). Neko links Boehm GC (its LICENSE file also reproduces the GC licence).

notes: Numbers match the Scriptorium README table exactly (1.104 s vs 1.341 s, 'x01.2', rank 11 vs 12). Main shortcoming: the win is within run-to-run noise; bench.csv's other recorded session has Neko slower than Lua (2.458 s vs 2.359 s), and the project itself is deprecated upstream. Kept at B for consistency with the chibi-scheme, Pawn and Terra Scriptorium verdicts.

tier_reason: Independent third-party CI shootout (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark, 59 stars; v8-v7 suite code in v8-v7/, driver scripts/update.ts, results 10/5/2026) shows njs Score 721/950 vs Duktape 489/905 on ubuntu/macos-arm64; not A because the GitHub Actions runners' CPU models and compiler versions are not stated (njs is built by ahaoboy/njs-build build.sh with default configure options). B matches the ChakraCore and v8 verdicts on the same suite.

corrections.baseline: Duktape 2.99.99 (unreleased master, built by ahaoboy/duktape-build with Duktape's development Makefile, which uses -Os -fomit-frame-pointer -g) on ubuntu/macos-arm64; QuickJS 2026.06.04 is faster than njs in this suite
corrections.compiler_and_flags: njs built by ahaoboy/njs-build build.sh: git clone nginx/njs, ./configure --with-quickjs (Bellard QuickJS linked) with njs's default compiler options; Duktape built with -Os; compiler versions not stated
corrections.workload: Score is the sum over the v8-v7 benchmark suite (Richards, DeltaBlue, Crypto, RayTrace, EarleyBoyer, RegExp, Splay, NavierStokes), higher is better; each engine's shell runs the inlined dist/run.js once per daily CI run on GitHub Actions runners (ubuntu-latest, macos-latest arm64, windows-latest) and the result is published in the repo README (snapshot 10/5/2026, 4:04:34 AM). njs is invoked without an engine flag, so the built-in njs engine (not njs's QuickJS backend) is what is measured.
corrections.caveats: Engines are prebuilt through the suite owner's *-build repos or release binaries; compiler versions and CPU models are not stated (GitHub Actions runners), and each engine runs once per day with no variance reported. The measured binary reports njs 0.9.2, while nginx/njs is at 1.0.1 (tags 1.0.0 2026-06-23, 1.0.1 2026-08-20), and the njs README says the built-in njs engine has been deprecated since 1.0.0 in favour of the QuickJS engine, so the result measures a stale build of a deprecated engine; njs's recommended QuickJS backend is QuickJS itself (already listed), which outscores njs here (1217/1761). The Duktape baseline is an -Os build of unreleased master (2.99.99). On macos-arm64 the margin is only about 5% by score, njs loses 4 of 8 sub-benchmarks (Crypto 1215 vs 1257, RayTrace 684 vs 1032, RegExp 216 vs 244, Splay 1472 vs 2594) and its wall time is longer (50 s vs 46 s); on ubuntu it loses RegExp (113 vs 129). No njs build on Windows. The v8-v7 suite is old and partly micro-benchmark. njs is mainly an nginx module; libnjs exists for embedding but is not a general-purpose embedding library.

notes: Numbers match the README tables (ubuntu njs 721 vs duktape 489, macos-arm64 950 vs 905, quickjs 1217/1761). Main shortcomings: stale 0.9.2 binary of the built-in engine that upstream deprecated in 1.0.0, a -Os Duktape baseline, and a mixed macOS result (slower wall time, 4 of 8 sub-benchmarks lost).

tier_reason: Independent third-party CI shootout (ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark; v8-v7 suite code in v8-v7/, driver scripts/update.ts, results 10/5/2026) shows quanta Score 1068/1118/941 vs Duktape 489/905/371 on ubuntu/macos-arm64/windows; not A because the runners' CPU models are not stated and Quanta is taken as a prebuilt release binary whose compiler and flags are not given. B matches the ChakraCore and v8 verdicts on the same suite.

corrections.baseline: Duktape 2.99.99 (unreleased master, built by ahaoboy/duktape-build with Duktape's development Makefile, which uses -Os -fomit-frame-pointer -g) on ubuntu/macos-arm64, Duktape 2.7.0 release (Makefile.cmdline) on windows; QuickJS 2026.06.04 is faster than Quanta in this suite
corrections.stars_or_usage: 26 stars, 3 forks; v1.0.0 release (dated September 28 on the releases page)
corrections.caveats: Engines are prebuilt through the suite owner's *-build repos or taken as release binaries (Quanta has no build repo in the suite's info.json, so its release binary's compiler and flags are unknown); CPU models are not stated (GitHub Actions runners) and each engine runs once per day with no variance reported. The v8-v7 suite is old and partly micro-benchmark. The Duktape baseline is an -Os build (unreleased master 2.99.99 on ubuntu/macOS). On macos-arm64 the margin is about 1.2x by score and Quanta loses 3 of 8 sub-benchmarks (Crypto 912 vs 1257, RegExp 215 vs 244, Splay 2074 vs 2594) with equal wall time (46 s each); on ubuntu and windows it wins all eight. Quanta trails QuickJS on every platform and is much larger (5.6 MB executable vs Duktape 370 KB and QuickJS 1 MB on ubuntu). Very young project (26 stars); v1.0.0 was released shortly before this snapshot; the README links the same third-party daily benchmark and lists no numbers of its own. MPL-2.0 is file-level copyleft; bundled PCRE2 (BSD-3-Clause with exception, used for RegExp), mimalloc (MIT) and utf8proc (MIT plus the Unicode data licence) as submodules.

notes: Numbers match the README tables exactly (quanta 1068/1118/941, duktape 489/905/371, quickjs 1217/1761/1067). Record said 'still pre-1.0'; corrected: v1.0.0 is released and is the version measured. Main shortcomings: -Os Duktape baseline, mixed macOS sub-results, slower than QuickJS, unknown release-binary flags.
